630	===== extraction_relations
631	CREATE TABLE extraction_relations (
632	  relation_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
633	
634	  -- THE FIGURE THIS EDGE QUALIFIES. NOT NULL and a real FK -- an edge naming no source
635	  -- row describes nothing. No UNIQUE index touches this column alone: one extraction may
636	  -- carry several comparator edges (a ramp slope is both condition_on a run-length limit
637	  -- AND audited_against a code's stated maximum), and collapsing that to one row per
638	  -- extraction would force a choice this table exists to avoid forcing.
639	  from_extraction_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
640	
641	  -- WHAT KIND OF COMPARISON THIS EDGE IS. Eight values; the CHECK is the vocabulary
642	  -- (CLAUDE.md section 4) and this is only its meaning, one line each.
643	  --   tested_at        -- the source physically measured its subjects at/against this
644	  --                      referent -- REF-00973's four ramp slopes were each tested_at a
645	  --                      named gradient.
646	  --   audited_against  -- the source measured whether subjects could perform WITHIN a
647	  --                      referent's own stated limit, rather than measuring an
648	  --                      independent value -- REF-00971's "existing standards".
649	  --   confirms         -- an independent measurement agrees with the referent's value.
650	  --   insufficient     -- the source asserts the referent's value is NOT ENOUGH for the
651	  --                      population or task in question -- REF-00784's 10-100% figure.
652	  --   exceeds          -- the source asserts the referent's value is more than needed.
653	  --   delta_over       -- the source states an increment relative to a baseline rather
654	  --                      than an absolute figure -- REF-00976's "more than thirty
655	  --                      centimetres of enlargement over the surveyed stock".
656	  --   condition_on     -- this figure only holds given a second figure this project also
657	  --                      holds as a row -- a slope given its run-length limit.
658	  --   derived_from     -- this figure is computed from the referent, never read off a
659	  --                      source -- always paired with input_role below and always a row
660	  --                      referent, never a label; see the CHECK immediately following.
661	  relation            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (relation IN (
662	                        'tested_at', 'audited_against', 'confirms', 'insufficient',
663	                        'exceeds', 'delta_over', 'condition_on', 'derived_from')),
664	
665	  -- THE REFERENT, HALF A: a row this project already holds. Nullable -- see to_label.
666	  -- Self-joins to the same table this column sits on, which is why the identity CHECK
667	  -- below refuses an edge from a row to itself.
668	  to_extraction_id    INTEGER REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
669	
670	  -- THE REFERENT, HALF B: prose naming what to_extraction_id would otherwise point at,
671	  -- for a referent this project has not captured as its own row -- a code clause never
672	  -- extracted on its own parameter, a source's private baseline sample, or a referent the
673	  -- source itself never names. Exactly one of this column and to_extraction_id is set on
674	  -- every row; the CHECK enforcing that sits with the rest below, not here, because it
675	  -- names both columns together.
676	  to_label            TEXT,
677	
678	  -- WHAT SORT OF THING to_label NAMES, when it is set. Meaningless and left NULL when
679	  -- the referent is a row instead -- a row already carries this information in its own
680	  -- data.
681	  --   standard      -- a code, guideline or published standard's own stated figure.
682	  --   own_sample    -- the source's own baseline measurement of its own subjects or
683	  --                   stock, as in REF-00976's surveyed housing.
684	  --   prior_source  -- an earlier study or publication, distinct from a code and from the
685	  --                   citing source's own sample.
686	  --   unnamed       -- the source itself does not say what the referent is. See the
687	  --                   `stated` column: this value and 'unnamed' there always travel
688	  --                   together, by CHECK.
689	  to_kind             TEXT CHECK (to_kind IS NULL OR to_kind IN (
690	                        'standard', 'own_sample', 'prior_source', 'unnamed')),
691	
692	  -- HOW EXPLICITLY THE SOURCE ITSELF NAMES THE REFERENT -- independent of whether this
693	  -- project could resolve it to a row. NOT NULL: every edge takes a position on this.
694	  --   named     -- the source identifies the referent by name (a code number, an author,
695	  --              a described sample).
696	  --   unnamed   -- the source gestures at a referent ("existing standards") without
697	  --              naming which one. Never a row referent -- see the CHECK below; naming
698	  --              nothing is not the same claim as naming a specific row.
699	  --   inferred  -- the source names no referent at all and this project supplied one from
700	  --              context (a code the jurisdiction and date make unambiguous). The
701	  --              weakest of the three and the one most likely to need revisiting.
702	  stated              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (stated IN ('named', 'unnamed', 'inferred')),
703	
704	  -- WHICH SIDE OF A DERIVATION this edge supplies. Meaningful only for relation =
705	  -- 'derived_from', enforced by CHECK -- every other relation leaves it NULL.
706	  --   base    -- the starting figure the derived value is computed from.
707	  --   delta   -- the increment added to (or subtracted from) the base.
708	  --   factor  -- a multiplier applied to the base, for a derivation `v_derived_figure_check`
709	  --            does not itself recompute -- that view covers base+delta only; a
710	  --            factor-based derivation is a known residual, not a silent gap, recorded
711	  --            here rather than built speculatively (CLAUDE.md section 8).
712	  input_role          TEXT CHECK (input_role IS NULL OR input_role IN ('base', 'delta', 'factor')),
713	
714	  -- THE SOURCE'S OWN WORDS FOR THE COMPARISON, NOT NULL. Mirrors the verbatim discipline
715	  -- `observed_terms.context_quote` and `db.py add-extraction`'s required `--claim-text`
716	  -- already carry on this project's other judgment-stage rows: a comparator asserted with
717	  -- nothing of the source's own phrasing behind it is not a comparator this project has
718	  -- actually read.
719	  quote               TEXT NOT NULL,
720	
721	  notes               TEXT,
722	
723	  created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
724	  created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
725	
726	  -- An edge cannot compare a figure to itself.
727	  CHECK (to_extraction_id IS NULL OR to_extraction_id <> from_extraction_id),
728	
729	  -- The referent is named as a row or as a label; never as both at once and never as
730	  -- neither, or the edge would point at two things or at nothing.
731	  CHECK ((to_extraction_id IS NULL) <> (to_label IS NULL)),
732	
733	  -- You cannot be conditioned by, or computed from, a figure that does not exist as a
734	  -- row: condition_on and derived_from both require a resolvable to_extraction_id.
735	  CHECK (relation NOT IN ('condition_on', 'derived_from') OR to_extraction_id IS NOT NULL),
736	
737	  -- input_role names which side of a derivation this edge is, so it is meaningless
738	  -- outside relation = 'derived_from' and mandatory inside it.
739	  CHECK (
740	    (relation = 'derived_from' AND input_role IS NOT NULL)
741	    OR (relation <> 'derived_from' AND input_role IS NULL)
742	  ),
743	
744	  -- An unnamed referent cannot simultaneously be one specific known row: if the source
745	  -- does not say what it is, this project cannot have resolved it to a row either.
746	  CHECK (stated <> 'unnamed' OR to_extraction_id IS NULL),
747	
748	  -- Calling the referent's kind 'unnamed' is a claim about how the source stated it, so
749	  -- it must agree with the stated column rather than disagree with it.
750	  CHECK (to_kind IS NULL OR to_kind <> 'unnamed' OR stated = 'unnamed')
751	)

import sqlite3, yaml, collections as C
c = sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
st = yaml.safe_load(open('governance/stage-map.yaml'))['tables']
T = [r[0] for r in c.execute("select name from sqlite_master where type='table' and name not like 'sqlite_%'")]
fk = [(t, f[3], f[2]) for t in T for f in c.execute(f'pragma foreign_key_list("{t}")')]
cols = {t: c.execute(f'pragma table_info("{t}")').fetchall() for t in T}
home = C.defaultdict(set)
for t in T:
    pk = [r[1] for r in cols[t] if r[5]]
    if len(pk) == 1: home[pk[0]].add(t)
adj = C.defaultdict(set)
for a, _, b in fk: adj[a].add(b); adj[b].add(a)
def bfs(s, goal, via_base):
    seen, q = {s: 0}, C.deque([s])
    while q:
        n = q.popleft()
        if n != s and goal(n): return seen[n]
        if n != s and not via_base and st.get(n) == 'base': continue
        for m in adj[n] - seen.keys(): seen[m] = seen[n] + 1; q.append(m)
bad = C.Counter(r[0] for r in c.execute('pragma foreign_key_check'))
nfail=0
for t in sorted(T, key=lambda t: (st.get(t, '?'), t)):
    fkc = {col for a, col, _ in fk if a == t}
    loose = [r[1] for r in cols[t] if r[1] in home and t not in home[r[1]] and r[1] not in fkc]
    up = 0 if st.get(t) == 'base' else bfs(t, lambda n: st.get(n) == 'base', True)
    dn = 0 if t == 'specifications' else bfs(t, lambda n: n == 'specifications', st.get(t) == 'base')
    fail = [d for d, v in (('up', up), ('down', dn)) if v is None] + ['orphan'] * (not adj[t]) \
         + [f'dangling:{bad[t]}'] * bool(bad[t]) + [f'unFK:{",".join(loose)}'] * bool(loose)
    if fail: nfail+=1; print(t, st.get(t, 'UNMAPPED'), '-' if up is None else up, '-' if dn is None else dn, ' '.join(fail) or 'ok', sep='\t')
print('FAILING', nfail, 'of', len(T), '; dangling total', sum(bad.values()))
PY

=== standards 2164-2192
---

CORRECTION to the three rulings recorded 2026-08-27 (`base_building`, `base_taxonomy_*`, underscore).
Raised by the R2 ruling-precedence audit; appended rather than edited, per append-only discipline.

**M1 — "§R8's substance survives in full… exactly as ruled" OVERCLAIMS, and the gap would be filled
silently.** The register-entry half is correct: the seven entries (`axes`, `axis_code`,
`item_axis_links`, `population_axis_map`, `access_need_axis_map`, `serves_axes`, `attaches_axes`)
name what is **retired**, so they are noun-independent and unaffected. **But the 08-25 ruling also
selected a derived FAMILY of replacement names** — `demand_code`, `item_demand_links`,
`population_demand_map`, `access_need_demand_map`, `serves_demands`, `attaches_demands`. The owner's
new words supply only **`base_taxonomy_icf`**, which replaces the head table and leaves **six
companion replacement names orphaned**. **They are REOPENED, not settled.** Whoever writes the rename
migration must derive them from the new head noun or put them to the owner — not invent them in
passing. *(`base_taxonomy_icf_links`? `item_icf_links`? Unresolved.)*

**D1 — two rows were completed from the note's enumeration and were not labelled as such.** The owner
said *"base_taxonomy_icf, base_taxonomy_medical etc"*. `base_taxonomy_identity` (← `populations`) and
`base_taxonomy_needs` (← `access_needs`) are **completions of the note's own verbatim list**, which is

VERDICT: **NO** — the design cannot be reached from the live data without stranding admitted evidence, two of its stated derivations are false on the live rows, and it removes a guard the book depends on (identifier reissue) while naming no replacement. Six HIGH, eleven MEDIUM, nine LOW findings below, worst first. Object: `/home/user/guidebook/workplan/pipeline-state-graph/IDEAL-GRAPH.md` (untracked). Scratch artefacts (not in repo): `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/db856d85-2082-5d35-9529-aa996506261b/scratchpad/{ideal.sql,ideal.db,live.db,reach.py,reach.db,chain.py,atoms_cited.tsv}`. The repo DB sha256 `d30f99ff…` was unchanged throughout; nothing was written into the repo.

---

## HIGH

**H1. Reachability: the ideal strands 28 of 53 admitted sources, 30 of 88 observations and 25–101 of 101 extractions.** (IDEAL-GRAPH.md:273-274, :283-284, :303-304, :314-315, :593)
Claim: "`retrievals` with NOT NULL pointers" from `evidence_sources`, `observed_terms`, `scans`; "a row with no bytes cannot meet the NOT NULL pointer and is re-read, not migrated. [GAP: how many can be linked is not measured.]"
Command: `python3 $S/reach.py` (row-by-row INSERT of every live counterpart into a fresh build of the §3 DDL, `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF`, then `PRAGMA foreign_key_check`). Trimmed:
```
evidence_sources (strict retrieval)   live=53 inserted=25  13x NOT NULL source_type; 15x NOT NULL retrieval_id
  sources: 53; with a strict (ref_id key + 2xx/exit0) payload: 38; any mention: 42; none: 11
  sources with no mention: REF-00987 00990 00991 00992 00994 00995 00996 00997 00998 01012 01014
observed_terms (retrieval via source)  live=88 inserted=58  30x NOT NULL retrieval_id
scans (synthesized per ref,slug,method) live=54 inserted=39 15x NOT NULL retrieval_id
source_value_extractions (raw: no scans on main) live=101 inserted=0  101x NOT NULL scan_id
source_value_extractions (scan synthesized)       live=101 inserted=101 → 25 dangling (scan_id,ref_id) / 19 under loose mapping
```
What is true: `scans` has 0 rows on `main` (T1 branch only), so every extraction fails `scan_id NOT NULL` as written; synthesising one scan per (ref, slug, method) still strands 25 extractions (19 if any manifest *mention* counts as bytes) because their sources have no persisted payload. `source_type` is NULL on 25 of 53 live sources (`q "select count(*) from evidence_sources where source_type is null"` → 25). The measurable gap the document left unmeasured: 11 sources have no manifest line anywhere; the document's "49 of 53" (c4b) used `file_anchor`, the wrong index — manifests carry `ref_id` on 80 lines and name 42 of 53 sources. "Re-read, not migrated" conflicts with LED-169/LED-170 (retire in place, never hard-delete: a row that cannot exist in the target schema is deleted by omission), with rule 3's append-only history (the rows' INSERTs stay in `scripts/migrations/data_*.sql` and `migration_reproducibility` would count them), and re-reading 11–15 sources is research work, not a tooling PR (rule 10). For REF-00997/00998 (Co-1-anchored determinations retired on them, see `retirement_reason` of specs 5–6) the Co-1 warrant row would vanish until re-read.

**H2. A33 / §10 "search_admissions … derived" is false: 48 of 55 admission edges are not derivable from candidates.** (:110, :872)
Claim: "`results_admitted` … derived: count of ADMITTED candidates of the search"; `search_admissions` "derived or DELETE".
Command: `q "select count(*) from search_admissions"` → 55; `q "select count(*) from search_admissions a where exists(select 1 from search_candidates k where k.exec_id=a.exec_id and k.resolved_ref_id=a.ref_id)"` → **7**; `q "select sum(results_admitted) from search_executions"` → 65; sources admitted with no resolving candidate: **44 of 51**.
What is true: the edge exec→source lives only in `search_admissions` for 44 admitted sources; deleting it leaves `v_follow_up`, `v_coverage`-based bucket refusal (A31) and LED-188's `results_admitted` with 7 of 65 admissions. The ideal has no column to migrate those 48 edges into (`search_candidates.exec_id` + `resolved_ref_id` would need 48 synthetic ADMITTED candidate rows with no title/quote/retrieval, violating `add-candidate`'s own guard).

**H3. A35's plan for the 14 non-derivable `source_slug_links` is infeasible under the ideal's own DDL.** (:112, :244, :876)
Claim: "the other 14 become `kind='locator'` PROMOTED rows in the compensating migration."
Command: `q "select ref_id, slug from source_slug_links l where not exists(...)"` → 14 rows, **6 distinct ref_ids; REF-00977, REF-00999, REF-01000, REF-01001 each appear twice**; 1 overlaps an existing `source_locators.ref_id`.
What is true: `search_candidates.ref_id TEXT UNIQUE` (:244) refuses the second row of each pair (8 rows) and the overlap (1 row); the fact being preserved — a second slug for one source — has no column (`suggested_slug` holds one). PROMOTED also forces `resolved_ref_id NOT NULL` (:254) on rows that were never candidates.

**H4. A32's derived `v_follow_up` mis-tags ~46 of 54 live preliminary extractions.** (:109, :469-474, :590)
Claim: "the tag is derived: `v_follow_up` lists preliminary extractions read under a slug the source was not admitted under."
Command: `q "select count(*) from source_value_extractions where extraction_status='preliminary'"` → 54; of these, source has an ADMITTED candidate resolving to it → **8**; extractions whose slug equals a slug the source was admitted under via `search_admissions` → 53.
What is true: the view's NOT-IN subquery reads `search_candidates.resolved_ref_id` only; for 44 of 51 admitted sources that set is empty, so every preliminary extraction of theirs appears as a cross-slug follow-up although 53 of 54 were read under their admitted slug. LED-201's "tagged for follow-up" would be applied to the wrong rows on day one; T1's explicit `extraction_follow_ups` (which A32 says "is not needed") does not have this failure.

**H5. PIP-17 "never reissue an identifier" loses both of its mechanisms and gets no replacement.** (:185, :314, :330, :394; §9 drops `identifier_floor_audit`)
Command: `grep -c AUTOINCREMENT $S/ideal.sql` → **0**; live: `['item_population_elaborations','gap_mining','evidence_source_authors','extraction_relations','base_parameters','determination_gates','specifications','source_value_extractions','population_icf_links']`; `sed -n 418,420p` of live `base_parameters` DDL: "AUTOINCREMENT (076): never reissue a parameter_id. Eleven data migrations on disk name parameter_id 1 and 2"; `scripts/audit/identifier_floor_audit.py:8-9,25`: "identifier … is computed as MAX+1 over the live tables … AUTOINCREMENT on the two integer keys (migration 076). Both are floors"; `dbcore.next_ref_id` = `ref_id_high_water(conn)+1`.
What is true: the ideal drops AUTOINCREMENT from `base_parameters`, `specifications`, `source_value_extractions`, `extraction_relations`, deletes the blocking floor audit, and names no CHECK/FK/writer that holds the invariant. K08 ("never hard-delete") is a norm; the audit exists because the norm was broken (item layer emptied, migration 057). Wrong thing reaching the book: `parameter_id 1` coming to mean something other than ramp gradient while eleven immutable migrations still say it does.

**H6. The synthesis merge (A03/A14/A25) cannot take the live synthesis rows.** (:80, :375-378, :881)
Claim: "`syntheses` + `synthesis_inputs` replace eight synthesis tables"; "only its weighting roles survive".
Command (reach.py): `synthesis_inputs<-convergence_sources live=110 inserted=0  46x CHECK role IN (...); 64x UNIQUE (synthesis_id, extraction_id)`; `spec_extraction_links on specs with NO convergence_id: 23`; `syntheses<-gaps(EG) 1x CHECK closed gap needs four fields (GAP-010)`.
What is true: `convergence_sources.role` is per *source* (`clinical` 21, `co1` 10, `discounted` 38); the ideal's input is per *extraction* with a different vocabulary. Mapping a source to its extractions (69→110 rows) collides on PK with the same extraction's `governing/conditioning/excluded` role from `specification_extraction_links` (64 collisions) and 46 rows carry a role the CHECK refuses. Specifications 1–3 (pending, `convergence_id NULL`, `gap_register_id` set) have 23 extraction links and no synthesis to hang them on — the ideal says a pending cell "carries a gap" synthesis, but the gap→synthesis id map and the link→gap attachment are not in the design. GAP-010 (CLOSED-DECIDED, all four closure fields NULL) violates the closed-gap CHECK. Also L3: counting one extraction twice under two roles is what the PK collision is refusing.

**H7. K22/LED-162 loses its mechanism: `extraction_relations` drops `input_role`, `to_kind` (25 live rows) and collapses `stated`.** (:330-334, :350)
Claim: "`add-extraction` … `derived_from` needs a base"; serves K22 ("a derived figure's band is floor(mean band ordinal)").
Command: `q "select relation, input_role, count(*) from extraction_relations group by 1,2"` → `input_role` NULL on all 36 today (no `derived_from` yet); `q "select count(*) from extraction_relations where to_kind is not null"` → 25; chain.py: `stated stored as: [('named','text')]` into `stated INTEGER NOT NULL`; `scripts/audit/extraction_relations_integrity.py` check 2: "Every figure_role='derived' row carries an outgoing … edge with relation='derived_from' AND input_role='base'"; check 3 reads `v_derived_figure_check`, which is not among the five views.
What is true: there is no column to say which input is the base and which the delta, so neither the writer rule the document states nor the band arithmetic LED-162 rules can be expressed; 25 rows' `to_kind` (standard/own_sample/prior_source/unnamed) and the three-valued `stated` (named 28 / unnamed 6 / inferred 2) are judgment facts that would have to be re-judged.

## MEDIUM

**M1. "12 gates kept" — five of them read objects the ideal deletes, so they are rewrites, unsized; and every test is deleted.** (:137, :804-815, :854, :887)
Command: references in kept scripts — `scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py` (1,522 lines): citation_mining ×9, found_under_slug, `tier` ×25; `scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py` (625): source_slug_links ×8, citation_mining ×8, items ×14; `scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py` (1,855): source_slug_links ×10, data_capture_status ×8, search_admissions ×11, `tier` ×21; `provenance_artefact_audit.py`: search_execution_artefacts ×2; `retrieval_log.py` (author_fidelity, 1,874): search_execution_artefacts ×4. §9's FILE list has no test file; the registry's 11 `test_*` entries and `scripts/tests/` (6,398 lines, `workplan/2026-10-12-simplification-workplan.md:18`) go with them, including `test_assess_cell_pilot` and `test_evidence_cell_state` — the engine the ideal makes the only writer of `specifications` would have no test.

**M2. Rule 10: the path cannot be tooling-only PRs.** (:890)
Claim: "Prune in place, by forward migrations, in tooling PRs ordered along the spine."
What is true (from H1–H3 and the specs row below): re-retrieving 11–15 sources, supplying `source_type` for 25 sources and `title` for 343 locators (`q "select count(*) from source_locators where title is null"` → 343), computing a `marker` for 5 retired provisional determinations (no band code exists: `grep -n -i 'band\|marker' scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` shows none that computes one), writing 14 PROMOTED rows and appending O1–O8 to the owner ledger (A30) are research/content acts. Precedent for the UPDATE half of A26 exists (`grep -l '^UPDATE' scripts/migrations/data_*.sql | wc -l` → 96; `emit_data_migration.py:52` handles UPDATE), so A26 itself is rule-3 compliant.

**M3. A36 rewrites a ratified MUST with no later owner statement and sits in §2, not §12.** (:113)
RES-12 (`governance/research-contract.yaml:239`, RATIFIED_DOC): "Case studies, economics and code values go to their structured tables … never prose notes." `grep -rniE 'economics|case stud' sessions/ references/project-standards.md | grep -i ruled` → no owner ruling superseding it. The document's own tie-break order is T1 > T2 > T3; A36 is decided by T3 against a ratified rule, which the document's §2 preamble says belongs in §12 ("Doctrine questions … are in §12, not here"). The document itself marks it CONFIDENCE medium and "I did not read the economics volume".

**M4. A23 adjudicates an OPEN owner question.** (:100) LED-202 is `OPEN` in ATOMS.tsv ("Whether a preliminary-status full-read figure may set a published value is unsettled"; `references/project-standards.md:4401` D1c). The design then builds `v_follow_up` and the engine's governing rule on the adopted side.

**M5. A12/A27 mint companion registry names the ledger says are reopened and owner-pending.** (:89, :104, :197)
